title: अंश २ · अध्याय १३

items.speaker: श्रीमैत्रेय उवाच
items.text:
भगवन् ! सम्यगाख्यातं यत् पृष्टोऽसि मयाखलम् ।
भूसमुद्रादिसरितां संस्थानं ग्रहसंस्थितिम् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
bhagavan ! samyagākhyātaṃ yat pṛṣṭo'si mayākhalam |
bhūsamudrādisaritāṃ saṃsthānaṃ grahasaṃsthitim || 1 ||

items.text:
विष्णवाधारं तथा चैतत् त्रैलोक्यं समवस्थितम् ।
परमार्थस्तु तेनोक्तो यथाज्ञानं प्रधानतः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
viṣṇavādhāraṃ tathā caitat trailokyaṃ samavasthitam |
paramārthastu tenokto yathājñānaṃ pradhānataḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
यत्त्वोतद्भगवानाह भरतस्य महीपतेः ।
कथयिष्यामि चरितं तन्माख्यातुमर्हसि ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
yattvotadbhagavānāha bharatasya mahīpateḥ |
kathayiṣyāmi caritaṃ tanmākhyātumarhasi || 3 ||

items.text:
भरतः स महीपालः शालग्रामेऽवसत् किल
योगयुक्तः समाधाय वासुदेवे सदा मनः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
bharataḥ sa mahīpālaḥ śālagrāme'vasat kila
yogayuktaḥ samādhāya vāsudeve sadā manaḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
पुण्यदेशप्रभावेण ध्यायतश्व सदा हरिम् ।
कथन्तु नाभवन्मुक्तिर्यदभूत् स द्रिजः पुनः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
puṇyadeśaprabhāveṇa dhyāyataśva sadā harim |
kathantu nābhavanmuktiryadabhūt sa drijaḥ punaḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
विप्रत्वे च कृतं तेन यद्भूयःसुमहात्मना ।
भरतेन मुनिश्वेष्ठ! तत् सर्व्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
vipratve ca kṛtaṃ tena yadbhūyaḥsumahātmanā |
bharatena muniśveṣṭha! tat sarvvaṃ vaktumarhasi || 6 ||

items.text:
पराशार अवाच ।
शालग्रामे महाभागो भगवन्नयस्तमानसः ।
स उवास चिरं कालं मैत्रेय! पृथिवीपतिः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
parāśāra avāca |
śālagrāme mahābhāgo bhagavannayastamānasaḥ |
sa uvāsa ciraṃ kālaṃ maitreya! pṛthivīpatiḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
अहिंसादिष्वशेषेषु गुणेषु गुणिनां वरः ।
अवाप परमां काष्ठां मनसश्चापि संयमे ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
ahiṃsādiṣvaśeṣeṣu guṇeṣu guṇināṃ varaḥ |
avāpa paramāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ manasaścāpi saṃyame || 8 ||

items.text:
यज्ञेशाच्युत गोविन्द माधवानन्त केशव !
कृष्णा विष्णो ह्टषीकेशेत्याह राजा स केवलम् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
yajñeśācyuta govinda mādhavānanta keśava !
kṛṣṇā viṣṇo hṭaṣīkeśetyāha rājā sa kevalam || 9 ||

items.text:
नान्यज्जागाद मैत्रेय! किञ्चित् स्वप्नान्तरेऽपि च ।
एततूपरं तदर्थञ्च विना नान्यदचिन्तयत् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
nānyajjāgāda maitreya! kiñcit svapnāntare'pi ca |
etatūparaṃ tadarthañca vinā nānyadacintayat || 10 ||

items.text:
समित्-पुष्प-कुशादानं चक्र देवक्रियाकृते ।
नान्यानि चक्र कर्म्माणि निः सङ्गो योगतापसः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
samit-puṣpa-kuśādānaṃ cakra devakriyākṛte |
nānyāni cakra karmmāṇi niḥ saṅgo yogatāpasaḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
जगाम सोऽबिषेकार्थमेकदा तु महानदीम् ।
सस्नौ तत्र तदा चक्र स्नानस्यनन्तरक्रियाः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
jagāma so'biṣekārthamekadā tu mahānadīm |
sasnau tatra tadā cakra snānasyanantarakriyāḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
अथातजगाम तत्तीर्थं जलं पात् पिपासिता ।
आसन्नप्रसवा ब्रह्मन्नेकैव हरिणी वनात् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
athātajagāma tattīrthaṃ jalaṃ pāt pipāsitā |
āsannaprasavā brahmannekaiva hariṇī vanāt || 13 ||

items.text:
ततः समभवत्तत्र पीतप्राय जले तया ।
सिंहस्य नादः सुमहान् सर्व्वप्राणिभयङ्करः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ samabhavattatra pītaprāya jale tayā |
siṃhasya nādaḥ sumahān sarvvaprāṇibhayaṅkaraḥ || 14 ||

items.text:
ततः सा सहसा त्रासादाप्लुता निम्नगातटम् ।
अत्युज्वारोहणेनास्या नद्यां गर्भः पपात सः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sā sahasā trāsādāplutā nimnagātaṭam |
atyujvārohaṇenāsyā nadyāṃ garbhaḥ papāta saḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
तमुह्ममानं वेगेन वीचिमालापरिप्लुतम् ।
तजग्राह स नृपो गर्भात् पतितं मृगपोतकम् ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
tamuhmamānaṃ vegena vīcimālāpariplutam |
tajagrāha sa nṛpo garbhāt patitaṃ mṛgapotakam || 16 ||

items.text:
गर्भप्रव्युतिदोषेण प्रोत्तुङ्गाक्रमणोन च ।
मैत्रेय! सापि हरिणी पपात च ममार च ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
garbhapravyutidoṣeṇa prottuṅgākramaṇona ca |
maitreya! sāpi hariṇī papāta ca mamāra ca || 17 ||

items.text:
हरिणीं तां विलोक्याथ विपन्नां नृपतापसः ।
मृगपोतं समादाय निजमाश्वममागतः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
hariṇīṃ tāṃ vilokyātha vipannāṃ nṛpatāpasaḥ |
mṛgapotaṃ samādāya nijamāśvamamāgataḥ || 18 ||

items.text:
चकारानुदिनञ्चासौ मृगपोतस्यवै नृपः ।
पोषण पुष्यमाणश्य स तेन वबृधे मुने ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
cakārānudinañcāsau mṛgapotasyavai nṛpaḥ |
poṣaṇa puṣyamāṇaśya sa tena vabṛdhe mune || 19 ||

items.text:
चचाराश्रमपर्य्यन्तं तृणानि गहनेषु सः ।
दूरं गत्वा च शाद्दूलत्रासादभ्याययौ पुनः ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
cacārāśramaparyyantaṃ tṛṇāni gahaneṣu saḥ |
dūraṃ gatvā ca śāddūlatrāsādabhyāyayau punaḥ || 20 ||

items.text:
प्रातर्गत्वातिदूरञ्च सायमायाद यथाश्वमम् ।
पुनश्च भरतस्याभूदाश्वमस्योटजाजिरे ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
prātargatvātidūrañca sāyamāyāda yathāśvamam |
punaśca bharatasyābhūdāśvamasyoṭajājire || 21 ||

items.text:
तस्य तस्मिन्मृगे दूर-समीपपरिवर्त्तिनि ।
आसीच्चेतः समायुक्तं न ययावन्यतो द्रिज ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
tasya tasminmṛge dūra-samīpaparivarttini |
āsīccetaḥ samāyuktaṃ na yayāvanyato drija || 22 ||

items.text:
विमुक्तराज्यतनयः प्रोज्झिताशेषबान्धवः ।
ममत्वं स चकारोच्चैस्तस्मिन् हरिणबालके ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
vimuktarājyatanayaḥ projjhitāśeṣabāndhavaḥ |
mamatvaṃ sa cakāroccaistasmin hariṇabālake || 23 ||

items.text:
किं वृकैक्भक्षितो व्याघूः किं सिंहेन निपातितः ।
चिरायमाणे निष्कान्ते तस्यासीदिति मानसम् ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
kiṃ vṛkaikbhakṣito vyāghūḥ kiṃ siṃhena nipātitaḥ |
cirāyamāṇe niṣkānte tasyāsīditi mānasam || 24 ||

items.text:
एषा वसुमती तस्य खुराग्रक्षतकर्बुरा ।
प्रीतये मम जातोऽसौ क्व ममैणकबालकः ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
eṣā vasumatī tasya khurāgrakṣatakarburā |
prītaye mama jāto'sau kva mamaiṇakabālakaḥ || 25 ||

items.text:
विषाणाग्रण मदूबाहुकण्डूयनपरो हि सः ।
क्षेमेणाभ्यागतोऽरण्यादिपि मां सुखयिष्यति ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
viṣāṇāgraṇa madūbāhukaṇḍūyanaparo hi saḥ |
kṣemeṇābhyāgato'raṇyādipi māṃ sukhayiṣyati || 26 ||

items.text:
एते लूनशिखास्तस्य दशनैरचिरोदूगतैः ।
कुशाः कासा विराजन्ते वटवः सामगा इव ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
ete lūnaśikhāstasya daśanairacirodūgataiḥ |
kuśāḥ kāsā virājante vaṭavaḥ sāmagā iva || 27 ||

items.text:
इत्थं चिरगते तस्मिन् स चक्र मानसं मुनिः ।
प्रीतिप्रसन्नवदनः पार्श्वस्थे चाभवन्मृगे ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
itthaṃ ciragate tasmin sa cakra mānasaṃ muniḥ |
prītiprasannavadanaḥ pārśvasthe cābhavanmṛge || 28 ||

items.text:
समाधिभङ्गस्तासीत् तन्ममत्वादृतात्मनः ।
सन्त्यक्तराज्यभोगर्द्धिखजनस्यापि भूपतेः ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
samādhibhaṅgastāsīt tanmamatvādṛtātmanaḥ |
santyaktarājyabhogarddhikhajanasyāpi bhūpateḥ || 29 ||

items.text:
चपलं चपले तस्मिन् दूरगं दूरगामिनि ।
मृगपतोऽभवज्वित्तं स्थैर्य्यवत्तस्य भूपतेः ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
capalaṃ capale tasmin dūragaṃ dūragāmini |
mṛgapato'bhavajvittaṃ sthairyyavattasya bhūpateḥ || 30 ||

items.text:
कालेन गच्छता सोऽथ कालञ्चक्र महीपतिः ।
पितेव सास्त्रं पुत्रेण मृगपोतेन वीक्षितः ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
kālena gacchatā so'tha kālañcakra mahīpatiḥ |
piteva sāstraṃ putreṇa mṛgapotena vīkṣitaḥ || 31 ||

items.text:
मृगमेव तदाद्राक्षीत् त्यजन् प्राणानसावपि ।
तन्मयत्वेन मैत्रय! नान्यत् किञ्चिदचिन्तयत् ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
mṛgameva tadādrākṣīt tyajan prāṇānasāvapi |
tanmayatvena maitraya! nānyat kiñcidacintayat || 32 ||

items.text:
ततश्व तत्कालकृतां भावनां प्राप्य तादृशीम् ।
जम्बूमार्गे महारण्ये जातो जातिस्मरो मृगः ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
tataśva tatkālakṛtāṃ bhāvanāṃ prāpya tādṛśīm |
jambūmārge mahāraṇye jāto jātismaro mṛgaḥ || 33 ||

items.text:
जातिस्मरत्वादुद्रिग्नः संसारस्य द्रिजोत्तम!
विहाय मातरं भूयः शालग्राममुपाययौ ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
jātismaratvādudrignaḥ saṃsārasya drijottama!
vihāya mātaraṃ bhūyaḥ śālagrāmamupāyayau || 34 ||

items.text:
शुष्कैस्तृणैस्तथा पर्णौः स कुर्व्वन्नात्मपोषणम् ।
मृगत्वहतुभूतस्य कर्म्मणो निष्कृतिं ययौ ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
śuṣkaistṛṇaistathā parṇauḥ sa kurvvannātmapoṣaṇam |
mṛgatvahatubhūtasya karmmaṇo niṣkṛtiṃ yayau || 35 ||

items.text:
तत्र चोतसृष्टदेहोऽसौ जज्ञ जातिस्मरो द्रिजः ।
सदाचारवतां शुद्ध योगिनां प्रवरे कुले ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
tatra cotasṛṣṭadeho'sau jajña jātismaro drijaḥ |
sadācāravatāṃ śuddha yogināṃ pravare kule || 36 ||

items.text:
अर्व्वविज्ञानसम्पन्नः सर्व्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्ववित् ।
अपश्यत् स च मैत्रेय ! आत्मानं प्रकृतेः परम् ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
arvvavijñānasampannaḥ sarvvaśāstrārthatattvavit |
apaśyat sa ca maitreya ! ātmānaṃ prakṛteḥ param || 37 ||

items.text:
आत्मनोऽधिगतज्ञानो देवादीनि महामुने ।
सर्व्वभूतान्यभेदेन स ददर्श महामतिः ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
ātmano'dhigatajñāno devādīni mahāmune |
sarvvabhūtānyabhedena sa dadarśa mahāmatiḥ || 38 ||

items.text:
न पपाठ गुरुप्रोक्तं कृतोपनयनः श्वुतिम् ।
न ददर्श च कर्माणि शास्त्रणि जगृहे न च ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
na papāṭha guruproktaṃ kṛtopanayanaḥ śvutim |
na dadarśa ca karmāṇi śāstraṇi jagṛhe na ca || 39 ||

items.text:
उक्तोऽपि बहुशः किञ्चिड़वाक्यमभाषत ।
तदप्यसंस्कारगुणां ग्राम्यवाक्योक्तिसंश्रितम् ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
ukto'pi bahuśaḥ kiñciṛavākyamabhāṣata |
tadapyasaṃskāraguṇāṃ grāmyavākyoktisaṃśritam || 40 ||

items.text:
अपध्वस्तवपुः सोऽपि मलिनाम्बरधृग् द्रिजः ।
क्लिन्नदन्तान्तरः सर्वैः परिभूतः स नागरैः ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
apadhvastavapuḥ so'pi malināmbaradhṛg drijaḥ |
klinnadantāntaraḥ sarvaiḥ paribhūtaḥ sa nāgaraiḥ || 41 ||

items.text:
सम्मानना परां हानिं योगर्द्धेः कुरुते यतः ।
जनेनावमतो योगी योगसिद्धिञ्च विन्दति ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
sammānanā parāṃ hāniṃ yogarddheḥ kurute yataḥ |
janenāvamato yogī yogasiddhiñca vindati || 42 ||

items.text:
तस्माज्वरेत वै योगी सतां मार्गमदूषयन् ।
जना यथावमन्येरन् गच्छयुर्नैव सङ्गतिम् ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
tasmājvareta vai yogī satāṃ mārgamadūṣayan |
janā yathāvamanyeran gacchayurnaiva saṅgatim || 43 ||

items.text:
हिरण्यगर्भवचनं विचिन्त्येत्थं महामतिः ।
आत्मानं दर्शयामास जडोन्मत्ताकृतिं जने ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
hiraṇyagarbhavacanaṃ vicintyetthaṃ mahāmatiḥ |
ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa jaḍonmattākṛtiṃ jane || 44 ||

items.text:
भुहूक्ते कुलम्षव्रीह्मादिशाकं वन्यं फलं कणान् ।
यदू यदाप्रोति सुबहु तदत्ते कालसंयमम् ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr:
bhuhūkte kulamṣavrīhmādiśākaṃ vanyaṃ phalaṃ kaṇān |
yadū yadāproti subahu tadatte kālasaṃyamam || 45 ||

items.text:
पितर्युपरते सोऽथ भ्रातृ-भ्रातृव्य-बान्धवैः ।
कारितः क्षेत्रकर्मादि कदन्नाहारपोषितः ॥ ४६ ॥
items.tr:
pitaryuparate so'tha bhrātṛ-bhrātṛvya-bāndhavaiḥ |
kāritaḥ kṣetrakarmādi kadannāhārapoṣitaḥ || 46 ||

items.text:
स तूक्षपीनावयवो जद़कारी च कर्मणि ।
सर्वलोकोपकरणां बभूवाहारवेतनः ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr:
sa tūkṣapīnāvayavo jadakārī ca karmaṇi |
sarvalokopakaraṇāṃ babhūvāhāravetanaḥ || 47 ||

items.text:
[तं तादृशमसंस्कारं विप्राकृविचेष्टितम् ।
क्षत्ता पृषतराजस्य काल्यै पशुमकल्पयत् ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr:
[taṃ tādṛśamasaṃskāraṃ viprākṛviceṣṭitam |
kṣattā pṛṣatarājasya kālyai paśumakalpayat || 48 ||

items.text:
रात्रौ तं समलङकृत्य वैशसस्य विधानतः ।
अधिष्ठितं महाकाली ज्ञात्वा योगेश्वरं तथा ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr:
rātrau taṃ samalaṅakṛtya vaiśasasya vidhānataḥ |
adhiṣṭhitaṃ mahākālī jñātvā yogeśvaraṃ tathā || 49 ||

items.text:
ततः खड गं समादाय निशितं निशि सा तथा ।
क्षत्तार क्रूरकर्माणमच्छिनत् कण्ठमूलतः ।
स्वपार्षदयुता देवी पपौ रुधिरमुल्वणम् ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ khaḍa gaṃ samādāya niśitaṃ niśi sā tathā |
kṣattāra krūrakarmāṇamacchinat kaṇṭhamūlataḥ |
svapārṣadayutā devī papau rudhiramulvaṇam || 50 ||

items.text:
ततः सौवीरराजस्य प्रयातस्य महात्मनः ।
विष्टिकर्ताथ मन्येत विष्टियोग्योऽयमित्यपि ॥ ५१ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ sauvīrarājasya prayātasya mahātmanaḥ |
viṣṭikartātha manyeta viṣṭiyogyo'yamityapi || 51 ||

items.text:
तं तादृशं महात्मानं भस्मच्छन्नमिवानलम् ।]*
*[ एतदाकारबन्धनीदूयान्तर्गतबागः सर्वत्र पुस्तके न दृश्यते । श्रीधरेणाप्यस्य व्याख्या न कृता, अतः सर्वसम्मति शून्यत्वादयं बागो बन्धनीदूयगर्मै स्थापितः ।]
तं तादृशमसंस्कारं विप्राकृतिविचेष्टितम् ।
क्षत्ता सौवीरराजस्य विष्टियोग्यममन्यत ॥ ५२ ॥
items.tr:
taṃ tādṛśaṃ mahātmānaṃ bhasmacchannamivānalam |]*
*[ etadākārabandhanīdūyāntargatabāgaḥ sarvatra pustake na dṛśyate | śrīdhareṇāpyasya vyākhyā na kṛtā, ataḥ sarvasammati śūnyatvādayaṃ bāgo bandhanīdūyagarmai sthāpitaḥ |]
taṃ tādṛśamasaṃskāraṃ viprākṛtiviceṣṭitam |
kṣattā sauvīrarājasya viṣṭiyogyamamanyata || 52 ||

items.text:
स राजा शिविकारूढो गन्तूं कृतमतिर्द्रिज !
बभूवेक्षुमतीतीरे कपिलर्षेर्वराश्रमम् ॥ ५३ ॥
items.tr:
sa rājā śivikārūḍho gantūṃ kṛtamatirdrija !
babhūvekṣumatītīre kapilarṣervarāśramam || 53 ||

items.text:
श्रेयः किमत्र संसारे दुः खप्राये नृणामिति ।
प्रष्टुं तं मोक्षधर्मज्ञ कपिलाख्यं महामुनिम् ॥ ५४ ॥
items.tr:
śreyaḥ kimatra saṃsāre duḥ khaprāye nṛṇāmiti |
praṣṭuṃ taṃ mokṣadharmajña kapilākhyaṃ mahāmunim || 54 ||

items.text:
उवाह शिविकां तस्य क्षत्तुर्वचनचोदितः ।
नृणां विष्टिगृहीतानामन्येषां सोऽपि मध्यगः ॥ ५५ ॥
items.tr:
uvāha śivikāṃ tasya kṣatturvacanacoditaḥ |
nṛṇāṃ viṣṭigṛhītānāmanyeṣāṃ so'pi madhyagaḥ || 55 ||

items.text:
गृहीतो विष्टिना विप्रः सर्वज्ञानैकभाजनम् ।
जातिस्मणेऽसौ पापस्य क्षयकाम उवाह ताम् ॥ ५६ ॥
items.tr:
gṛhīto viṣṭinā vipraḥ sarvajñānaikabhājanam |
jātismaṇe'sau pāpasya kṣayakāma uvāha tām || 56 ||

items.text:
ययौ जड़गतिः सोऽथ युगमात्रवलोकनः ।
कुर्वन् मतिमतां श्रेष्ठस्तदन्ये त्वरितं ययुः ॥ ५७ ॥
items.tr:
yayau jaṛagatiḥ so'tha yugamātravalokanaḥ |
kurvan matimatāṃ śreṣṭhastadanye tvaritaṃ yayuḥ || 57 ||

items.text:
विलोक्य नृपतिः सोऽथ विषमां शिबिकागतिम् ।
किमेतदित्याह समं गम्यतां शिबिकावहाः ॥ ५८ ॥
items.tr:
vilokya nṛpatiḥ so'tha viṣamāṃ śibikāgatim |
kimetadityāha samaṃ gamyatāṃ śibikāvahāḥ || 58 ||

items.text:
पुनस्तथैव शिबिकां विलोक्य विषमां हि सः ।
नृपः किमेतदित्याह भवद भिर्गम्यतेऽन्यथा ॥ ५९ ॥
items.tr:
punastathaiva śibikāṃ vilokya viṣamāṃ hi saḥ |
nṛpaḥ kimetadityāha bhavada bhirgamyate'nyathā || 59 ||

items.text:
भूपतेर्वदतस्तस्य श्रुत्वेत्थं बहुशो वचः ।
शिबिकावाहकाः प्रोचुरयं यातीत्यसत्वरम् ॥ ६० ॥
items.tr:
bhūpatervadatastasya śrutvetthaṃ bahuśo vacaḥ |
śibikāvāhakāḥ procurayaṃ yātītyasatvaram || 60 ||

items.text:
किं श्रान्तोऽस्यल्पमद्वानं त्वयोढा शिहिका मम ।
किमायाससहो न त्वं पीनानसि निरीक्ष्यसे ॥ ६१ ॥
items.tr:
kiṃ śrānto'syalpamadvānaṃ tvayoḍhā śihikā mama |
kimāyāsasaho na tvaṃ pīnānasi nirīkṣyase || 61 ||

items.text:
नाहं पीवान्न चैवोढा शिबिका भवतो मया ।
न श्रान्तोऽस्मि न चायासः सोञव्योऽस्ति महीपते ॥ ६२ ॥
items.tr:
nāhaṃ pīvānna caivoḍhā śibikā bhavato mayā |
na śrānto'smi na cāyāsaḥ soñavyo'sti mahīpate || 62 ||

items.text:
प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यसे पीवानद्यांपि शिबिका त्वयि ।
श्रमश्व भारोदूहने भवत्येव हि देहिनाम् ॥ ६३ ॥
items.tr:
pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyase pīvānadyāṃpi śibikā tvayi |
śramaśva bhārodūhane bhavatyeva hi dehinām || 63 ||

items.text:
प्रत्यक्ष भवता भूप ! यदू दृष्ट मम तदूद ।
बलवानबलश्चेति वाच्यं पश्वादू विशेषणम् ॥ ६४ ॥
items.tr:
pratyakṣa bhavatā bhūpa ! yadū dṛṣṭa mama tadūda |
balavānabalaśceti vācyaṃ paśvādū viśeṣaṇam || 64 ||

items.text:
त्वयोढ़ा शिबिका चेति त्वय्यद्यापि च संस्थिता ।
मिथ्यैतदत्र तु भवाञ्छृणोतु वचनं मम ॥ ६५ ॥
items.tr:
tvayoṛhā śibikā ceti tvayyadyāpi ca saṃsthitā |
mithyaitadatra tu bhavāñchṛṇotu vacanaṃ mama || 65 ||

items.text:
भूमौ पादयुगस्यास्था जह्घ पाददूये स्थिते ।
ऊरू जङ्घादूयावस्थौ तदाधारं तथोदरम् ॥ ६६ ॥
items.tr:
bhūmau pādayugasyāsthā jahgha pādadūye sthite |
ūrū jaṅghādūyāvasthau tadādhāraṃ tathodaram || 66 ||

items.text:
वक्षः स्थलं तथा बाहू स्कन्धौ चोदरसंस्थितौ ।
स्कन्धाश्रितेयं शिबिका मम भारोऽत्र किकृतः ॥ ६७ ॥
items.tr:
vakṣaḥ sthalaṃ tathā bāhū skandhau codarasaṃsthitau |
skandhāśriteyaṃ śibikā mama bhāro'tra kikṛtaḥ || 67 ||

items.text:
शिबिकायां स्थितं चेदं वपुस्त्वदुपलक्षितम् ।
तत्र त्वमहमप्यत्र प्रोच्यते चेदमन्यथा ॥ ६८ ॥
items.tr:
śibikāyāṃ sthitaṃ cedaṃ vapustvadupalakṣitam |
tatra tvamahamapyatra procyate cedamanyathā || 68 ||

items.text:
अहं त्वञ्च तथान्ये च भूतैरुह्माम पार्थिव ।
गुणप्रवाहपतितो भूतवर्गोऽपि यात्ययम् ॥ ६९ ॥
items.tr:
ahaṃ tvañca tathānye ca bhūtairuhmāma pārthiva |
guṇapravāhapatito bhūtavargo'pi yātyayam || 69 ||

items.text:
कर्मवश्या गुणाश्चैते सत्त्वाद्या- पृथिवीपते !
अविद्यासञ्चितं कर्म्म तज्वाशेषेषु जन्तुषु ॥ ७० ॥
items.tr:
karmavaśyā guṇāścaite sattvādyā- pṛthivīpate !
avidyāsañcitaṃ karmma tajvāśeṣeṣu jantuṣu || 70 ||

items.text:
आत्मा शुद्धोऽक्षरः शान्तो निर्गुणः प्रकृतेः परः ।
प्रवृद्धयपचयौ नास्य एकस्याखिलजन्तुषु ॥ ७१ ॥
items.tr:
ātmā śuddho'kṣaraḥ śānto nirguṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ |
pravṛddhayapacayau nāsya ekasyākhilajantuṣu || 71 ||

items.text:
यदा नोपचयस्तस्य न चैवापचये नृप!
तदा पीवानसीतीत्थं कया युत्तया त्वयेरितम् ॥ ७२ ॥
items.tr:
yadā nopacayastasya na caivāpacaye nṛpa!
tadā pīvānasītītthaṃ kayā yuttayā tvayeritam || 72 ||

items.text:
भू-पाद-जङ्घा-क्ठ्यूरु-जठरादिषु संस्थिते ।
शिबिकेयं यता स्कन्धे तथा भारः समस्त्वया ॥ ७३ ॥
items.tr:
bhū-pāda-jaṅghā-kṭhyūru-jaṭharādiṣu saṃsthite |
śibikeyaṃ yatā skandhe tathā bhāraḥ samastvayā || 73 ||

items.text:
तदान्यैर्जन्तुभर्भूप ! शिबिकोढा न केवलम् ।
लै-द्रुम-गृहोत्थोऽपि पृथिवीसम्भवोऽपि वा ॥ ७४ ॥
items.tr:
tadānyairjantubharbhūpa ! śibikoḍhā na kevalam |
lai-druma-gṛhottho'pi pṛthivīsambhavo'pi vā || 74 ||

items.text:
यदा पुसः पृथग्भावः प्राकृतैः कारणौर्नृप !
सोढव्यस्तु तदायासः कथं वा नृपते । मया ॥ ७५ ॥
items.tr:
yadā pusaḥ pṛthagbhāvaḥ prākṛtaiḥ kāraṇaurnṛpa !
soḍhavyastu tadāyāsaḥ kathaṃ vā nṛpate | mayā || 75 ||

items.text:
यदूद्रव्या शिबिका चेयं तदूद्रव्यो भूतसंग्रहः ।
भवतो मेऽखिलस्यास्य ममत्वेनोपबृ हितः ॥ ७६ ॥
items.tr:
yadūdravyā śibikā ceyaṃ tadūdravyo bhūtasaṃgrahaḥ |
bhavato me'khilasyāsya mamatvenopabṛ hitaḥ || 76 ||

items.text:
एवमुक्त्वाभवन्मैनी स वहञ्छिबिकां द्रिज !
सोऽपि राजावतीर्य्योर्व्यं तत्पादौ जगृहे त्वरन् ॥ ७७ ॥
items.tr:
evamuktvābhavanmainī sa vahañchibikāṃ drija !
so'pi rājāvatīryyorvyaṃ tatpādau jagṛhe tvaran || 77 ||

items.text:
भो भो विसृज्य शिबिकां प्रसादं कुरु मे द्रिज!
कथ्यतां को भवानत्र जालमरूपधरः स्थितः ॥ ७८ ॥
items.tr:
bho bho visṛjya śibikāṃ prasādaṃ kuru me drija!
kathyatāṃ ko bhavānatra jālamarūpadharaḥ sthitaḥ || 78 ||

items.text:
यो भवान् यन्निमित्तं वा यदागमनकारण्म् ।
तत्सर्वं कथ्यतां विदून् ! मह्म शुश्रूषवे त्वया ॥ ७९ ॥
items.tr:
yo bhavān yannimittaṃ vā yadāgamanakāraṇm |
tatsarvaṃ kathyatāṃ vidūn ! mahma śuśrūṣave tvayā || 79 ||

items.text:
श्रूयतां कोऽहमित्येतदूक्तुं भूप! न शक्यते ।
उपभोगनिमित्तञ्च सर्वत्र गमनक्रिया ॥ ८० ॥
items.tr:
śrūyatāṃ ko'hamityetadūktuṃ bhūpa! na śakyate |
upabhoganimittañca sarvatra gamanakriyā || 80 ||

items.text:
सुखदुः खोपभोगौ तु तौ देहाद्यु पपादकौ ।
धर्माधर्मोद्भवौ भोक्तु जन्तुर्देहादिमृच्छति ॥ ८१ ॥
items.tr:
sukhaduḥ khopabhogau tu tau dehādyu papādakau |
dharmādharmodbhavau bhoktu janturdehādimṛcchati || 81 ||

items.text:
सर्वस्यैव हि बूपाल ! जन्तोः सर्वत्र कारणम् ।
धर्माधर्मौ यतः कस्मात् कारणां पृच्छयते त्वया ॥ ८२ ॥
items.tr:
sarvasyaiva hi būpāla ! jantoḥ sarvatra kāraṇam |
dharmādharmau yataḥ kasmāt kāraṇāṃ pṛcchayate tvayā || 82 ||

items.text:
धर्माधमां न सन्देहः सर्वकार्य्येषु कारणम् ।
उपभोगनिमित्तञ्च देहाद्द हान्तरागमः ॥ ८३ ॥
items.tr:
dharmādhamāṃ na sandehaḥ sarvakāryyeṣu kāraṇam |
upabhoganimittañca dehādda hāntarāgamaḥ || 83 ||

items.text:
यत्त्वैतद भवता प्रोक्त कोऽहमित्येतदात्मनः ।
वक्तु न शक्यते श्रोतु तन्ममेच्छा प्रवर्त्तते ॥ ८४ ॥
items.tr:
yattvaitada bhavatā prokta ko'hamityetadātmanaḥ |
vaktu na śakyate śrotu tanmamecchā pravarttate || 84 ||

items.text:
योऽस्ति सोऽहमिति ब्रह्मन्! कथं वक्तुं न शक्यते ।
आत्मन्येष न दोषाय शब्दोऽहमिति यो द्रिज ॥ ८५ ॥
items.tr:
yo'sti so'hamiti brahman! kathaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate |
ātmanyeṣa na doṣāya śabdo'hamiti yo drija || 85 ||

items.text:
शब्दोऽहमिति दोषाय आत्मन्येष तथैव तत् ।
अनात्मन्यात्मविज्ञानं शब्दो वा भ्रान्तिलक्षणाः ॥ ८६ ॥
items.tr:
śabdo'hamiti doṣāya ātmanyeṣa tathaiva tat |
anātmanyātmavijñānaṃ śabdo vā bhrāntilakṣaṇāḥ || 86 ||

items.text:
जिह्वा ब्रवीत्यहमिति दन्तोष्ठौ तालुक नृप!
एते नाहं यतः सर्वे वाङूनिष्पादनहेतवः ॥ ८७ ॥
items.tr:
jihvā bravītyahamiti dantoṣṭhau tāluka nṛpa!
ete nāhaṃ yataḥ sarve vāṅūniṣpādanahetavaḥ || 87 ||

items.text:
किंहेतुभिर्वदत्येषा वागेवाहमिति स्वयम् ।
तथापि वाग् नाहमेतद् वक्तु मित्थं न युज्यते ॥ ८८ ॥
items.tr:
kiṃhetubhirvadatyeṣā vāgevāhamiti svayam |
tathāpi vāg nāhametad vaktu mitthaṃ na yujyate || 88 ||

items.text:
पिण्डः पृथग् यतः पुसः शिरः पाण्यादिलक्षणाः ।
ततोऽहमिति कुत्रैतां संज्ञां राजन्! करोम्यहम् ॥ ८९ ॥
items.tr:
piṇḍaḥ pṛthag yataḥ pusaḥ śiraḥ pāṇyādilakṣaṇāḥ |
tato'hamiti kutraitāṃ saṃjñāṃ rājan! karomyaham || 89 ||

items.text:
यद्यन्योऽस्ति परः कोऽपि मत्तः पार्थिवसत्तम !
तदैषोऽहमयञ्चान्यो वक्तुमेवमपीष्यते ॥ ९० ॥
items.tr:
yadyanyo'sti paraḥ ko'pi mattaḥ pārthivasattama !
tadaiṣo'hamayañcānyo vaktumevamapīṣyate || 90 ||

items.text:
यदा समस्तदेहेषु पुमानेको व्यवस्थितः ।
तदा हि को भवान् कोऽहमित्येतद् विफलं वचः ॥ ९१ ॥
items.tr:
yadā samastadeheṣu pumāneko vyavasthitaḥ |
tadā hi ko bhavān ko'hamityetad viphalaṃ vacaḥ || 91 ||

items.text:
त्वं राजा शिबिका चेयमिमे वाहाः पुरः सराः ।
अयञ्च भवतो लोको न सदेतन्नृपोच्यते ॥ ९२ ॥
items.tr:
tvaṃ rājā śibikā ceyamime vāhāḥ puraḥ sarāḥ |
ayañca bhavato loko na sadetannṛpocyate || 92 ||

items.text:
वृक्षदू दारु ततश्चैयं शिबिका त्वदधिष्ठिता ।
किं वृक्षसंज्ञा वास्याः स्याद्दारुसंज्ञाथवा नृप ॥ ९३ ॥
items.tr:
vṛkṣadū dāru tataścaiyaṃ śibikā tvadadhiṣṭhitā |
kiṃ vṛkṣasaṃjñā vāsyāḥ syāddārusaṃjñāthavā nṛpa || 93 ||

items.text:
वृक्षारूढो महाराजो नायं वदति ते जनः ।
न च दारुणि सर्वस्त्वां ब्रवीति शिबिकागतम् ॥ ९४ ॥
items.tr:
vṛkṣārūḍho mahārājo nāyaṃ vadati te janaḥ |
na ca dāruṇi sarvastvāṃ bravīti śibikāgatam || 94 ||

items.text:
शिबिका दारुसङ्गातो रचनास्थितिसंस्थितः ।
आन्वष्यतां नृपश्वेष्ठ! तद्भदे शिबिका त्वया ॥ ९५ ॥
items.tr:
śibikā dārusaṅgāto racanāsthitisaṃsthitaḥ |
ānvaṣyatāṃ nṛpaśveṣṭha! tadbhade śibikā tvayā || 95 ||

items.text:
एवं छत्रशलाकानां पृथगूभागो विमृश्यताम् ।
क्व यातं छत्रमित्येष न्यायस्त्वयि तथा मयि ॥ ९६ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ chatraśalākānāṃ pṛthagūbhāgo vimṛśyatām |
kva yātaṃ chatramityeṣa nyāyastvayi tathā mayi || 96 ||

items.text:
पुमान् स्त्री गौरजो वाजी कुञ्जरो विहगस्तरुः ।
देहेषु लोकसंज्ञयं विज्ञया कर्म्महेतुषु ॥ ९७ ॥
items.tr:
pumān strī gaurajo vājī kuñjaro vihagastaruḥ |
deheṣu lokasaṃjñayaṃ vijñayā karmmahetuṣu || 97 ||

items.text:
पुमान्न देवो न नरो न पशुर्न च पादपः ।
शरीराकृतिबेदास्तु भूपैते कर्म्मयोनयः ॥ ९८ ॥
items.tr:
pumānna devo na naro na paśurna ca pādapaḥ |
śarīrākṛtibedāstu bhūpaite karmmayonayaḥ || 98 ||

items.text:
वस्तु राजेति यल्लोके यच्च राजभटात्मकम् ।
तथान्यज्व नृपेत्थं तन्न सत्सङ्कल्पनामयम् ॥ ९९ ॥
items.tr:
vastu rājeti yalloke yacca rājabhaṭātmakam |
tathānyajva nṛpetthaṃ tanna satsaṅkalpanāmayam || 99 ||

items.text:
यत्तु कालान्तरेणापि नान्यां संज्ञामुपैति वै ।
परिणामादिसम्भूतां तदूस्तु नृप! तज्व किम् ॥ १०० ॥
items.tr:
yattu kālāntareṇāpi nānyāṃ saṃjñāmupaiti vai |
pariṇāmādisambhūtāṃ tadūstu nṛpa! tajva kim || 100 ||

items.text:
त्वं राजा सर्व्वलोकस्य पितुः पुत्रो रिपो रिपुः ।
पत्न्याः पतिः पिता सूनोः किं त्वा भूप ! वदाम्यहम् ॥ १०१ ॥
items.tr:
tvaṃ rājā sarvvalokasya pituḥ putro ripo ripuḥ |
patnyāḥ patiḥ pitā sūnoḥ kiṃ tvā bhūpa ! vadāmyaham || 101 ||

items.text:
त्वं किमेतच्छिरः किं नु ग्रीवा तव तथोदरम् ।
किमु पादादिकं त्वं वा तवैतत् किं महीपते ॥ १०२ ॥
items.tr:
tvaṃ kimetacchiraḥ kiṃ nu grīvā tava tathodaram |
kimu pādādikaṃ tvaṃ vā tavaitat kiṃ mahīpate || 102 ||

items.text:
समस्तावयवेभ्यस्त्वं पृथग् भूप ! व्यवस्थितः ।
कोऽहमित्यत्र निपुणो भूत्वा चिन्तय पार्थिव ॥ १०३ ॥
items.tr:
samastāvayavebhyastvaṃ pṛthag bhūpa ! vyavasthitaḥ |
ko'hamityatra nipuṇo bhūtvā cintaya pārthiva || 103 ||

items.text:
एवं व्यवस्थिते तत्त्वे मयाहमिति भाषितुम् ।
पथक् करणनिष्पाद्य शक्यते नपते! कथम् ॥ १०४ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ vyavasthite tattve mayāhamiti bhāṣitum |
pathak karaṇaniṣpādya śakyate napate! katham || 104 ||

en_chapter: Maitreya said:—"O respected Sir, all that I ask of you, has been perfectly related by you, namely the situation of the earth, seas, mountains, rivers, and planets, the system of the three worlds of which Vishnu is the support; you have also related that the holy knowledge is pre-eminent. You said that you would relate the story of Bharata, the lord of the earth: it becomes you now to relate that. Bharata, the protector of the earth, lived at the holy pilgrimage of Sālagrām. And he was engaged in devotion with his mind ever attached to Vāsudeva. Living at a sacred place he was always devoted to Hari: Why then he failed to obtain final liberation, O twice-born one? And why was he born again as a Brahmin, O foremost of Munis? It becomes you to relate this".

Parāçara said:—The illustrious lord of the earth, O Maitreya, lived for a long time at Sālagrām having his mind wholly devoted to the glorious God. And having been considered, on account of his kindness and other virtues, the foremost of the virtuous, he secured in the highest degree, the entire control over his mind. The Raja was ever repeating the names Yajnesa, Achyuta, Govinda, Mādhava, Ananta, Keshava, Krishna, Vishnu, Hrishikesa. And nothing else than this did he utter even in his dreams: nor did he meditate upon anything, but those names and their significance. He accepted fuel, flowers and holy grass for the worship of the deity and did he celebrate no other religious observance being entirely given to disinterested abstract devotion.

One day he went to the river Mahānadi for the purpose of ablution. And having bathed there he engaged in after ceremonies. Whilst thus engaged there came to the same spot a doe big with young who had come out of the forest to drink of the stream. Whilst the doe was drinking there was audible a dreadful uproar of a lion capable of striking terror into all creatures. Thereupon, the doe, greatly terrified, jumped out of the water on the banks; on account of this great leap her fawn was suddenly brought forth and fell into the river. And beholding it carried away by the stream the king suddenly caught hold of the young one and saved it from being drowned. The injury which the doe had received on account of the violent exertion proved fatal. She lay down and died. Having observed this the royal ascetic took the fawn in his arms and came back to the hermitage. There he fed it and nursed it every day: and under his fostering care it throve and grew up. It frolicked about the hermitage and grazed upon the grass in its neighbourhood. And sometimes afraid of a tiger it used to come to the ascetic. In this wise the young one sometimes wandered far away in the morning and came back to the hermitage in the evening and frolicked in the leafy bower of Bharata.

His mind, O twice-born one, was thus attached to that animal, playing either in the neighbourhood or at some distance and he was unable to think of anything else. And the king, although he had severed all bonds of attachments towards his friends, his kingdom, his son and wife, grew inordinately attached to this fawn. When absent for an unusually long time he would think that it had been carried away by wolves, devoured by a tiger or slain by a lion. He used to cry out,—'The earth is embrowned with the prints of its hoofs. What has become of the fawn that was born for my delight? How happy I should become if he had come back from the forest. I felt his budding antlers rubbing against my arm. These tufts, of sacred grass, the heads of which have been nibbed by his new teeth, look like pious lads chanting the Shama-Veda.'

Whenever this fawn used to absent itself for a long time from the hermitage the ascetic would think thus. And he was delighted and his countenance grew animated whenever it neared him. His mind being thus engrossed by the fawn his abstraction was interrupted although he had renounced family, wealth and kingdom. His mind became unsettled with the wanderings of the fawn. Whenever it wandered away to a great distance the king's mind followed it and when it was silent his mind became settled. Thus in the course of time the king became subject to its influences and was watched by the deer with tearful eyes like a son mourning for the father. And the king, when he died, saw the young fawn only before him; and having his mind engrossed by him, O Maitreya, he did not see anything else.

On account of such feeling at such an hour he was born again in Jambumarga forest as a deer with the faculty of recollecting his former life. Cherishing a distaste for the world on account of this recollection he left his mother and again repaired to holy place of Salagram. Living there upon dry grass and leaves he expatiated the acts which had led to his being born in such a condition: and upon his death he was born as a Brahmin still retaining the recollection of his former life. He was born in a devout and illustrious family of ascetics who rigidly observed devotional practices. Having been gifted with true knowledge and acquainted with the spirit of all sacred writings he observed soul as contra-distinguished from Prakriti (matter). And acquainted with the knowledge of self he observed the celestial and all other beings as the same. When he was invested with the Brahminical thread he did not read the Vedas with a preceptor, did not perform the ceremonies nor did he read the scriptures. And requested again and again he replied incoherently in ungrammatical and unpolished speech. His body was unclean and he used to wear dirty clothes. Saliva dribbled from his mouth and he was treated with hatred by the people. Undue respect from the people obstructs abstraction and hence the ascetics, disregarded by people, attain to the consummation of their asceticism. Without polluting the way treaded by the saints the ascetics should so behave that the ordinary folk might hate them and not come in their company. Having thus thought of this saying (Bharata) gifted with high intellect assumed the appearance of a crazy idiot in the eyes of the people. He used to live on raw pulse, potherbs, wild fruit and grains of corn and whatever came in his way as a part of necessary but temporary infliction.

On the death of his father he was set to work in the field by his brothers and nephews and fed by them with wretched food. He was firm and stout like a bull and used to act like a simpleton and people used to make him work and give him food only as his wages.

Once on a time the gate-keeper of the king of Sauvira, regarding him as an idle uneducated Brahmin, considered him a worthy person to work without pay and took him into his master's service to assist in carrying the palanquin. One day O Brahman, the king wished to go in palanquin to the hermitage of the great sage Kapila, situated on the banks of the river Ikshumati, to consult the sage, who was conversant with the virtues leading to liberation, what as most desirable in a world abounding with care and sorrow. And he was one of those, who had, at the order of the head servant, been compelled to carry the palanquin gratuitously. And that Brahman, gifted with the only universal knowledge and recollecting former birth, although compelled to do this, bore the burden as the means of expatiating the sins for which was desirous to atone. While the other bearers proceeded with alacrity, he, fixing his eyes upon the pole, moved tardily. And perceiving the palanquin carried unevenly the king exclaimed 'Ho bearers! what is this? keep equal space.' Still it went on unsteadily and the king again cried out. ‘What is this? How irregularly are you going?' When this had again and again taken place the palanquin bearers at last replied to the king, 'It is this man who lags in his space.' ‘How is this' said the king to the Brahmin, 'Are you exhausted? You have carried your burden only a little way. Are you unable to bear exhaustion? But you look very robust' To which the Brahmin replied—‘It is not I, O king, who am robust nor is it I who carry your palanquin. I am not exhausted, O king! nor am I capable of fatigue.' The king said, ‘I distinctly perceive that you are stout and the palanquin is carried by you, and a heavy burden is wearisome to all persons.' The Brahmin said: ‘Tell me first what you have distinctly seen of me and then you may distinguish my properties as strong or weak. The statement, that you behold the palanquin borne by me or placed on me, is unreal. Listen, O king, to my arguments about it. Both the feet are placed on the ground: the legs are supported by the feet; the thighs rest upon the legs; and the belly rests upon the thighs; the chest is supported by the belly and the arms and shoulders are supported by the chest; the palanquin is carried by the shoulders and then how can it be considered as my burden? This body which is seated in the palanquin is known as "thou" thence what is elsewhere called this is here distinguished as thou and I. I and thou and others are made of elements and elements, influenced by qualities, assume a bodily shape. Qualities depend on acts, and acts perpetrated in ignorance influence the condition of all beings. The soul is pure, imperishable, tranquil, devoid of qualities, distinct from nature and is without increase or diminution; and if it is freed from increase or diminution then with what prosperity you say to me, ‘I see that you are robust? If the palanquin is placed on the body, the body on the feet, the feet the ground, then the burden is carried as much by you as by me. Why are not others, O king, feeling the burden of this palanquin. If I am exhausted with a burden that is being carried on another's shoulder, then why with the weight of this palanquin, people may be worn out with the weight of mountains, trees, houses and even of the earth, When the nature of men is different, either in its essence or its cause, then it may be said that fatigue is to be undergone by me. The material, with which the palanquin is made, is the substance of you and me and of all others being a collection of Elements collected by individuality.'

Parāçara said:—Having said this the Brahman became silent and went on carrying the palanquin; the king too speedily got down from it and touched his feet. The king said: O Brahman, leave off the palanquin and be propitiated with me. Tell me who art thou under the disguise of a fool? The Brahman replied "Hear me, king. Who I am it is not possible to say; I go anywhere for receiving the fruits of good and bad luck. The body is produced for the enjoyment of pleasure and endurance of pain. Pleasure and pain originate from virtue and vice; therefore the soul assumes bodily shape for enjoying pleasure and enduring pain consequent upon virtue and vice. The universal cause of all living creatures is virtue or vice, why therefore enquire after the cause of my coming to this earth."

The king said:—"That virtue and vice are the causes of all actions and that people migrate into various bodies for receiving their consequences, there is not the least doubt about it; but as regards what you have said that it is not possible for you to say who you are, it is a matter which I wish to have explained. O Brahman, how cannot a man declare himself to be that which he (really) is: there can be no harm to one's self from applying to it the word 'I'".

The Brahmana said:—"To use the word ‘I' undoubtedly is detrimental; but it is not improperly used if it is applied merely to the soul. But the term is erroneous in as much as it conceives that to be the self or soul which is not self or soul. The tongue articulates the word ‘I' assisted by the lips, the teeth and the palate; and these are the origin of the expression, as they are the causes of the production of speech.

"If by these instruments speech can utter the word 'I' it is not at all proper to say that speech itself is ‘I.' O king, the body of a man having hands, feet and other limbs is composed of various parts: to what part shall we apply the word ‘I'? If another being had existed in this body quite different from me, then it may be said, O king, that this is I, that is the other; while one soul inhabits the whole body, then such questions as 'Who are you? Who am I?' are useless. Thou art a monarch; this is a palanquin: these are the bearers: these are thy followers; yet it is untrue that these are thine. This palanquin, in which thou art seated, is made of timber got from trees. Then tell me, what name, tree, timber or palanquin, shall be applied to it, O king. The people shall not say that their monarch is seated on a tree or on a timber but they shall say that he is in the palanquin. The artificial assemblage of the pieces of timber is called the palanquin: judge yourself, therefore, O king, in what the palanquin differs from the wood. Again consider the sticks of the umbrella, in their separate state. What then is the umbrella? Apply this argument to thee and to me. A man, a woman, a cow, a goat, a horse, an elephant, a bird, a tree, are names given to various bodies, which they assume on account of their primitive actions. Man is neither a god, nor a man, nor a beast, nor a tree: these are the various shapes which he assumes on account of his acts. O king, your name is Vasuraja and another name is Rajabhat—besides you have got various other names—but none of these names is real and is nothing but the work of imagination. And what thing is there in the world, O king, which being subject to changes, does not in the course of time, go by different names? You are called the king of the world, the son of your father, the enemy of your foes, the husband of your wife, the father of your children, what name the shall I apply to you? What is your situation? Are you the head or the belly? Or are they yours? Are you the feet or are they yours? You are, O king, separate in nature from the members of your body. Then considering properly, do you think who I am. And since the truth has been got at, how is it possible for me to recognize the distinction and to apply to my individual the expression 'I'".
